title: Why doesn't Callable use -> for return types?
author: MYmichelle
duncathan
text:
This is a good question! As you guessed, there is indeed a technical reason. Python’s type annotations are always valid Python expressions - there’s not actually any unique syntax within them. If you wanted to, you could do myvar = Callable[[float, float], float] and that would assign that value to myvar. The arrow syntax can only be used in a function definition statement, which is not a valid Python expression; therefore it can’t be used directly when working with Callable.
That being said: you have probably noticed that Callable is sometimes awkward to use for certain functions. In cases like that, callback protocols can be used to represent more complex function types, and has syntax much more closely linked to normal function definitions (since this one is defined with a function definition, itself!)
